editorial:
Imagine being on a school trip and suddenly waking up in a hospital with no idea why you collapsed. That is exactly what happens to Stephanie, a teenager who finds out she just gave birth without even knowing she was pregnant. Things go from bad to worse when a baby's body is found, and the police are convinced she killed her own child. You will feel the stress building up as she tries to fight a legal system that has already decided she is a monster. It is a heavy story, but it keeps you glued to the screen because you just want to know if she can prove her innocence.

The acting is the best part here, as you really feel the pain and confusion of a girl whose life is falling apart. The pacing is steady, though some of the court scenes might feel a bit slow if you are looking for a thriller. If you like true crime stories that make you think about how unfair the world can be, you should definitely check this out. It is a tough watch, but it stays with you long after the credits roll.
endingExplained: In the end, the movie shows that Stephanie was telling the truth about not knowing she was pregnant. The legal battle is a struggle, but the truth eventually comes out about her mental state and the tragedy of the situation. She does not get a happy fairy tale ending, but she finally finds some peace. The movie wraps up by showing how the system failed her and the trauma she had to carry.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gripping court dramas and true stories about injustice.
